newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama Canal traffic back to normal after backlog.
newsitem.headline: Panama Canal traffic back to normal after backlog.

text.p: Traffic through the Panama Canal has returned to normal after weeks of severe backlog that had been caused by the sinking of a commercial tugboat, officials said on Wednesday.
"All traffic levels and booking procedures are back to normal," a Panama Canal Commission (PCC) spokeswoman said.
"By midnight tonight we're expecting 22 vessels awaiting transit, and 21 vessels by midnight tomorrow," she said.
PCC officials are still investigating what caused the tug boat San Pablo II to sink on April 21 while assisting in dredging work at the approach of one of the canal's Pacific Coast locks.
It created a backlog of as many as 100 vessels awaiting transit. The tug boat was removed on April 28.
"They have had some hearings on the case, but nothing has been finalized. The findings are not expected for another few weeks," the spokeswoman said.
